subject: Palisade Systems: sudden throughput & p99 spike after v4.1 quant profile
messages:
From: Ben Wallace <ben.w@palisade.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Production degradation after v4.1 quant profile deploy

Sergio —

We started seeing a severe throughput drop starting ~08:45 PDT and p99 latencies jumped from ~180ms to 1.2s across our hot endpoints. Error rates (5xx) for the inference route are up ~3x. We rolled no changes on our side; I believe you shipped the new v4.1 quant profile last night.

I attached a tar of logs and a hotspot trace (hotpath-trace-20260628.html). Can you confirm whether this is related to the latest quantization? This is impacting our checkout flow. We need ETA on mitigation.

Ben Wallace
Head of Engineering, Palisade Systems
ben.w@palisade.com

Attachments: palisade-logs-20260628.tar.gz, hotpath-trace-20260628.html

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Wallace <ben.w@palisade.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation after v4.1 quant profile deploy

Ben — thanks for the quick heads up and the artifacts. We're seeing correlated signals in our telemetry for the same time window.

Immediate plan:
- I'll coordinate a short canary rollback to the previous quant profile (v3.8) on a small subset of Palisade traffic to confirm impact (5 minute window).
- Engineering (Hannah + Marcus) will run a targeted hotpath trace and validate tokenization delta.
- I'll loop in our reliability lead Monica and CS lead Rishi to keep Palisade in the loop.

Can you authorize a 5-minute canary rollback on 10% of traffic? If yes, we can start within 20 minutes.

Sergio Alvarez
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Sergio@redwood.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation after v4.1 quant profile deploy (internal)

Internal notes (quick triage):
- Telemetry shows a 40% increase in model decode time on p95+ for sequences > 128 tokens starting 08:43 PDT.
- Memory and GPU utilization are nominal; root cause looks like changed tokenization length distribution + a qprofile path that falls back to slower kernels for particular attention patterns.
- Hotpath trace shows more KV cache churn; quantized matmul kernels in v4.1 use a different tiling that appears to underperform for Palisade's typical batch/seq mix.

Mitigation options:
1) Canary rollback to qprofile v3.8 (expected: restore baseline in ~2 minutes for canary traffic). Low risk.
2) Adjust serving runtime fallback to force alternative matmul kernel for affected shard (requires deploy and 30–45m to validate).

Recommend option 1 to buy time and then schedule option 2 as follow-up if regression persists. I'll prepare the rollback playbook now.

— Hannah
Staff SRE, Runtime Performance

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Wallace <ben.w@palisade.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@palisade.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation after v4.1 quant profile deploy

Ben / Priya —

Thanks for confirming. We propose the following immediate steps:
1) Canary rollback: flip 10% of Palisade traffic back to quant profile v3.8 for 5 minutes and monitor throughput, p99, and error rate.
2) If canary shows restoration, we will expand to 50% then 100% with 5–10 minute watch windows.
3) Parallel: deep diagnostic run by runtime team to identify kernel/tiling mismatch and a postmortem.

Please reply with GO to authorize the canary. We plan to run the rollback starting at 10:55 PDT.

Sergio
Director, Customer Success

priya.sharma@palisade.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Ben Wallace <ben.w@palisade.com>, Priya Sharma <priya.sharma@palisade.com>
Date: 2026-06-29T17:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production degradation after v4.1 quant profile deploy — rollback complete and metrics

Summary / post-canonical update:
- We executed a staged rollback to qprofile v3.8 on 2026-06-28 per the canary plan; initial canary (10%) restored p99 from ~1.2s -> 190ms and reduced 5xx by >90% within 90s. We then ramped to 100% over 20 minutes.
- Current metrics (last 1h): throughput back to baseline, p99 stable ~185–220ms, error rate within SLA. See attached metrics-spike-06-28.png for before/after.
- Root cause hypothesis: qprofile v4.1 introduced a tiling/kernelling path that underperforms for Palisade's token-length distribution, causing increased KV churn and suboptimal matmul kernels.

Next steps (we commit to):
- Engineering deep-dive and reproducible test by 2026-06-30 23:59 PDT.
- Patch candidate (forcing alternate matmul kernel) or refined qprofile v4.1.1 by 2026-07-03.
- Joint postmortem with Palisade on 2026-07-01 10:00 PDT.

We appreciate Palisade's patience and will follow up with the postmortem. If you want an exec-level sync before the joint postmortem, looping in Laura Bennett and Evelyn Hart for scheduling.

— Marcus Lin
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

Attachments: metrics-spike-06-28.png
